one_liner: Google's advertising platform API for programmatically creating, managing, and reporting on Google Ads campaigns.
self_serve_evidence: Test/Explorer access levels are auto-granted self-serve, but Basic Access (~5 business days) and Standard Access (~10 business days, unlimited quota) require a developer-token application reviewed via the API Center, with brand verification possible.
api_surface: REST and gRPC API using Google Ads Query Language (GAQL); broad surface covering campaigns, ad groups, keywords, billing, reporting across dozens of resources/services.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Google-maintained server at github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp (search, resource metadata, list_accessible_customers tools, OAuth/ADC auth).
blocker: Developer token approval (Basic/Standard access) required for production use beyond limited Explorer/test tiers; process takes 5-10 business days and requires manager account setup.
notes: Explorer access (auto-granted) is enough for light production use at low volume (2,880 ops/day); serious agent tooling will need Basic Access at minimum.

one_liner: Meta's Marketing API for creating, managing, and analyzing Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns.
self_serve_evidence: Full Access (formerly Advanced Access, needed for real ads_management usage) requires App Review plus demonstrating 500+ Marketing API calls in 15 days with <15% error rate; default Limited Access has low rate limits.
api_surface: REST-style Graph API; broad surface covering campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, audiences, insights/reporting, catalogs, and Conversions API.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers (135 tools in some); no official Meta-maintained MCP found.
blocker: App Review / Full Access tier gating requires prior usage history and passing Meta's review, which is a real approval gate for production ad management.
notes: System User tokens (non-expiring) make server-to-server automation feasible once access tier is approved.

one_liner: LinkedIn's Marketing API suite for managing ad campaigns, lead sync, audience targeting, and conversion tracking.
self_serve_evidence: Only baseline permissions (profile, email, w_member_social) are self-serve; the Advertising API product requires applying through the Developer Portal and becoming an approved partner, with Matched Audiences requiring approved partner status.
api_surface: REST APIs spanning campaign management, reporting/analytics, Lead Sync, Matched Audiences, Conversions API, and company/community management — moderately broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community servers exist; no official LinkedIn MCP found.
blocker: Marketing API access is not self-serve — it requires formal partner-program application and approval by LinkedIn, with no guaranteed timeline.
notes: This is one of the strictest gates among the 10 apps studied; approval is discretionary and relationship-based, not purely criteria-based like Google/Meta.

one_liner: All-in-one CRM/marketing automation platform (funnels, CRM, calendars, SMS/email) for agencies and SMBs.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can instantly sign up on the Marketplace developer portal, create an app, and receive OAuth2 Client ID/Secret immediately for Private app use; public Marketplace listing is optional and only reviewed at that later stage.
api_surface: REST API (v2) covering CRM/contacts, opportunities/pipelines, calendars/appointments, messaging (SMS/email/calls), payments, workflows, and 50+ webhook events — broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Numerous community MCP servers with OAuth support; no official HighLevel MCP found.
notes: Private integration tokens are also supported as a simpler non-OAuth auth alternative for single-account use.

one_liner: Email marketing and marketing automation platform for building campaigns and managing subscriber audiences.
self_serve_evidence: Any logged-in account holder can generate an API key immediately from account settings and start calling the API; OAuth2 is available for multi-account apps without a gated review step to obtain it.
api_surface: REST Marketing API covering campaigns, audiences/lists, automations, reports, templates, and e-commerce data — broad and mature.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community servers (112 tools in some); no official Mailchimp-maintained MCP found.
notes: API access can be limited by the authorizing user's account role, but this is account-level, not a platform approval gate.

one_liner: E-commerce-focused email and SMS marketing automation platform with customer data and event tracking.
self_serve_evidence: Private and public API keys are generated instantly and self-serve from account Settings with custom scopes; OAuth is only gated at the point of formal App Marketplace listing, not for basic API use.
api_surface: REST (JSON:API spec) covering 20+ resource categories — profiles, events, campaigns, flows, catalogs, metrics, coupons, forms, webhooks — with filtering, sparse fieldsets, and versioned releases; broad and modern.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Klaviyo-maintained MCP server, documented at developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server, offering hosted/local deployment and read-only/restricted modes.
notes: Having an official first-party MCP server makes this one of the most agent-ready apps in the set.

one_liner: All-in-one funnel builder and marketing platform (funnels, email, courses, affiliate management) for online businesses.
self_serve_evidence: Users generate a Public API key directly from dashboard profile settings and immediately authenticate via the X-API-Key header — no application or review process.
api_surface: REST API (cursor-paginated, JSON merge-patch support) covering contacts, tags, and related resources; narrower/still-evolving surface compared to larger platforms, with OAuth planned but not yet available.
existing_mcp_detail: Official systeme.io-hosted MCP server covering contacts, newsletters, funnels, price plans/coupons, and automation rules via MCP keys.
notes: API surface is comparatively narrow (contacts/tags-focused per current public docs) even though access itself is frictionless; official MCP already exists, which is notable for a smaller SaaS.

one_liner: Visual discovery/social platform API for managing pins, boards, ads, and analytics.
self_serve_evidence: Trial access (sandbox-only, self-serve after app registration with privacy policy) is the default, but Standard/production access requires submitting a video demonstration of the OAuth flow for manual review.
api_surface: REST API (v5) covering pins, boards, ads, audiences, catalogs, and user account management; moderately broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community servers exist; no official Pinterest MCP found.
blocker: Standard (production, non-sandbox) access requires a manual video-review approval process; Trial access limits all created content to sandbox-only visibility.
notes: Even single-user/internal integrations must complete the video-review step to escape the sandbox restriction, per Pinterest's own docs.

one_liner: Meta's Threads API for publishing posts, replies, and reading insights on the Threads text-based social app.
self_serve_evidence: threads_basic requires no review, but content publishing, reply management/reading, and insights permissions all require Meta App Review before any non-tester account can use them.
api_surface: REST-style Graph API surface covering post publishing, replies, insights/analytics; narrower than the full Facebook/Instagram Graph API but growing.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community servers exist; no official Meta-maintained Threads MCP found.
blocker: App Review is required for the permissions needed to actually publish/read content and insights for non-tester (real) users.
notes: Testers added under App Roles can use full functionality immediately without review, so prototyping/dev is unblocked even though public production use is gated.

one_liner: Twilio-owned transactional and marketing email delivery platform with an API for sending and managing email.
self_serve_evidence: Users create API keys instantly via account Settings and immediately authenticate with a Bearer token (or Basic Auth using 'apikey' as username) — no application/review step.
api_surface: REST v3 API covering transactional email sending, marketing campaigns, contacts/lists, templates, stats/analytics, and webhooks — broad and mature.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community servers exist; no official Twilio/SendGrid-maintained MCP found as of this research.
notes: One of the most frictionless integrations in this set — instant API key, well-documented REST surface, no approval gate.
